title: Ada and the Compass
premise: In 1898, Freya Galloway, daughter of a disgraced pearl diver and indentured to the Meridian Trading Company in a remote Australian port, has learned that survival means being unremarkable. When a scarred stranger named Tobias Ash arrives carrying letters in her father's handwriting—letters written after his supposed drowning at sea—Freya discovers her father faked his death to escape the company's debts and left evidence that could expose Meridian's trafficking in indentured islanders. As the company closes in, Freya, her ailing mother, and Tobias must decide who takes the last berth on a departing ship: the father who abandoned them, the mother who sacrificed everything, or the truth itself, carried in a stolen ledger. Freya ultimately gives up her own place, sends her mother and the ledger to justice in Sydney, and stays behind to face the company—choosing truth over loyalty, and discovering that history has always been happening to her.
about_author: E. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial shipping records in northern Australia. Their fascination with the erased lives of indentured laborers informs a debut that blends meticulous research with intimate family drama.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Freya Galloway, POV. Freya dives for pearl shell under Meridian Trading Company contract, counting her father's debt in breathless minutes underwater. We learn her mother's worsening cough and Freya's philosophy: history belongs to admirals and company men, not to people like her. Emotional beat: quiet resignation masking a fierce, buried longing to matter.

chapters.title: Ledger Lines
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. At the company office, Freya copies debt figures and notices entries that don't add up—men listed as dead whose rations are still drawn. Her supervisor, Mr. Calloway, catches her looking and warns her with chilling courtesy that curiosity is a debt too. Emotional beat: first crack in her belief that invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: A Stranger at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Tobias Ash, POV. Tobias arrives in port with salt-scars and a satchel of letters, asking after the Galloway family. He watches Freya from the jetty, recognizing her father's eyes. He has crossed two oceans because a dying friend asked him to deliver proof. Emotional beat: dread and resolve in a man running out of time.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Tobias shows her the letters—her father's unmistakable slant, dated three years after his boat went down. Freya's grief curdles into rage: he chose to vanish and let them inherit his debt. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under everything she believed about her own family.

chapters.title: What the Mother Knew
chapters.summary: Maren Galloway, POV. Maren confesses she has known for two years—her husband sent money and a warning: never let Meridian learn he lives, or they'll come for all of you. She made Freya's invisibility a doctrine out of love. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as protection, and the cost of secrets kept too well.

chapters.title: The Island Manifest
chapters.summary: Freya and Tobias, alternating. Comparing the letters with office records, they realize the 'dead' divers are islanders Meridian sells onward as forced labor, their deaths faked on paper. Freya's father witnessed a drowning that wasn't an accident. Emotional beat: horror giving way to purpose—this is no longer about one family.

chapters.title: Calloway's Kindness
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Calloway unexpectedly reduces her debt, offers her mother medicine, and asks gentle questions about strangers in town. Freya understands the trap too late: kindness is his instrument. Emotional beat: the sickening recognition that she has already been measured and marked.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV. The supply ship Southern Cross departs in nine days with one berth Tobias has secured—passage to Sydney, where a reformist magistrate waits for evidence. One berth, three people who need it: Maren, whose lungs are failing; the father, whose testimony anchors the case; or the ledger itself. Emotional beat: arithmetic of sacrifice begins.

chapters.title: Night Dive
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Freya dives the wreck of her father's boat at night to retrieve the strongbox he hid there, nearly drowning when her line fouls. She surfaces with the box and a new understanding of the water that was supposed to kill him. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into claim—she will not be what the sea almost took.

chapters.title: The Father's Letters
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Inside the strongbox: the ledger page, a confession naming the company's buyer, and letters to Freya he never sent—tender, cowardly, full of excuses. She reads them all night. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together; forgiveness offered and not yet granted.

chapters.title: Where He Waits
chapters.summary: Freya and Tobias, POV. Tobias reveals the rendezvous: her father is hiding on Thursday Island, waiting to sail if Freya sends word. Freya must decide whether to summon the man who let them drown on land. Emotional beat: the pull of blood against the weight of abandonment.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. A neighbor's boy reports strangers at the Galloway house. Calloway posts men on the jetty and doubles the watch on Freya's family. Maren burns her husband's old letters to protect him, weeping as they curl. Emotional beat: the noose tightening; love expressed as destruction of the past.

chapters.title: Medicine for a Debt
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Calloway delivers the cough medicine personally, naming his price: the ledger and the stranger, by Friday. He speaks of her father with intimate contempt, revealing he was there the night the boat 'sank.' Emotional beat: cold fury crystallizing into a plan; fear stops being paralyzing.

chapters.title: A Map of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Freya, Tobias, and Maren plan by lamplight. They will copy the ledger, send the original north with the father's testimony, and split up so no one boat carries everything. Freya argues to take the berth herself; her mother quietly overrides her. Emotional beat: family as a war council, love as strategy.

chapters.title: The Copyist
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Freya forges Calloway's own hand to forge a requisition that gets her into the records room overnight, copying the trafficking entries page by page while Calloway dines above. Emotional beat: exhilarating transgression—the invisible girl rewriting the company's own history.

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV. Caught leaving the records room, Freya is saved when Tobias creates a diversion that ends with him arrested in her place. Through his cell window he sees Calloway telegraphing Sydney. Emotional beat: sacrifice and the terrible knowledge that the clock has run out.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Freya can free Tobias only by trading the ledger; she can save her mother only by using the berth. Calloway offers a third path: denounce her father publicly, and all debts are forgiven. She looks at her mother's hollowed face and understands the question was never which family member—it was which self survives. Emotional beat: the moral summit.

chapters.title: The Berth Given
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Freya puts her mother and the original ledger on the Southern Cross, gives her own berth money to buy Tobias's release, and sends word north for her father—knowing it may bring Calloway's men instead. On the jetty, Maren presses Freya's father's compass into her hand. Emotional beat: heartbreak as an act of agency.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Roads
chapters.summary: Tobias and Freya, POV. A cyclone stalls the Southern Cross in the roads; Calloway's men board to seize the ledger before she sails. In the chaos, the harbor master—whose brother was among the 'dead'—turns his boat across the company launch. Emotional beat: the community's silent loyalty surfacing at last.

chapters.title: The Man from the Sea
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Her father arrives through the storm's tail, ragged and unrepentant and finally present. He offers to surrender himself to draw Calloway's men off the ship. Freya gives him the compass and her silence—not forgiveness, but a debt of her own choosing. Emotional beat: severance and release in one gesture.

chapters.title: The Southern Cross Sails
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. The ship clears the reef with Maren and the ledger aboard as Calloway's warrant arrives too late. Freya stands on the jetty, arrested, certain she has lost everything—until the harbor master and half the divers' camp stand witness beside her, refusing to let her be invisible. Emotional beat: climax resolving into solidarity.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Months later, the Sydney trial topples Meridian's trade; Freya, freed on the harbor master's bond, receives her mother's letter and a newspaper clipping. She stays in the port, teaching divers' children their letters, keeping the copied ledger's twin hidden in her father's old strongbox. Emotional beat: quiet triumph—history happened to her, and now she writes it.
